page.layout: One block of text: a verse poem set in one column, under a running head. Page number at top right. Signature mark at the foot, centre and right.

p.i: Præsens qui placide pieq; seclum Vult transmittere, vir bonusq; haberi, Curis abstq; meris, molestiisq; Is ante omnia maximum Iehouam Sincere vereatur, atque amet, nec Non & ante oculos sibi reponat Verbi iussa salutis, exsequatur Gnauus officia & vocationis: Suum diligat intimoq; amore Proximum, pariter suas agat res: Non sese ἀλλοτρίοις det implicatum, Vt sortem placide ferat, vel unum Curet; diuitiis hiet ne opimis: Aulai atq; fori pericla mille Et discrimina sed [?]dolus vitabit: Immittet rigidos subinde frenos Linguæ, det labiis suis capistrum: Γλωσσαγώγος non agat perinde, Quod est esse velit, nihilq; malit, Esse quenq; sinat, quod est, simulq; Sic est ille futurus idem & usq; Tum cubilia vitet inquinare, Et thorum fugiat coinquinatum Purum a crimine corpus, & sagacem Conseruans animum, piumq; pectus, Infami abstineat manusq; furto, Sensus dirigat atq; cautus actus: Non sit alterius, suis licet dum Esse, nemine obesse, adesse cunctis: Hoc emblemata nostræ docebunt, Quod ipsum fauet aduouens Oraeus.

page.notes: Verse printed as one continuous poem; line breaks are not kept, lines are run together with spaces. Greek words (ἀλλοτρίοις; Γλωσσαγώγος) are doubtful in detail and should be checked against the scan. "sed [?]dolus" is a doubtful reading of a damaged word. "nihilq; malit" and "quenq;" are doubtful. The word "Oraeus" is as printed. Bottom right "EX" is a second signature mark, not transcribed as text. The printed "1" at top right is the page number.
